claim: Eukaryotic cells deploy autophagy to eliminate invading microbes.
source: Eukaryotic cells deploy autophagy to eliminate invading microbes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the role of autophagy in immunity.

claim: Pathogens have evolved effector proteins to counteract antimicrobial autophagy.
source: In turn, pathogens have evolved effector proteins to counteract antimicrobial autophagy.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about pathogen-host interactions.

claim: The Irish famine pathogen Phytophthora infestans secretes the effector protein PexRD54.
source: The Irish famine pathogen Phytophthora infestans secretes the effector protein PexRD54 that selectively activates an unknown plant autophagy pathway that antagonizes antimicrobial autophagy at the pathogen interface.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: PexRD54 selectively activates an unknown plant autophagy pathway that antagonizes antimicrobial autophagy at the pathogen interface.
source: The Irish famine pathogen Phytophthora infestans secretes the effector protein PexRD54 that selectively activates an unknown plant autophagy pathway that antagonizes antimicrobial autophagy at the pathogen interface.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: PexRD54 induces autophagosome formation by bridging vesicles decorated by the small GTPase Rab8a with autophagic compartments labeled by the core autophagy protein ATG8CL.
source: Here, we show that PexRD54 induces autophagosome formation by bridging vesicles decorated by the small GTPase Rab8a with autophagic compartments labeled by the core autophagy protein ATG8CL.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Rab8a is required for pathogen-triggered and starvation-induced but not antimicrobial autophagy.
source: Rab8a is required for pathogen-triggered and starvation-induced but not antimicrobial autophagy, revealing specific trafficking pathways underpin selective autophagy.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Specific trafficking pathways underpin selective autophagy.
source: Rab8a is required for pathogen-triggered and starvation-induced but not antimicrobial autophagy, revealing specific trafficking pathways underpin selective autophagy.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential requirement of Rab8a in different autophagy pathways.

claim: PexRD54 utilizes lipid droplets to facilitate biogenesis of autophagosomes diverted to pathogen feeding sites.
source: By subverting Rab8a-mediated vesicle trafficking, PexRD54 utilizes lipid droplets to facilitate biogenesis of autophagosomes diverted to pathogen feeding sites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: PexRD54 mimics starvation-induced autophagy to subvert endomembrane trafficking at the host-pathogen interface.
source: Altogether, we show that PexRD54 mimics starvation-induced autophagy to subvert endomembrane trafficking at the host-pathogen interface, revealing how effectors bridge distinct host compartments to expedite colonization.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Autophagy is a conserved eukaryotic cellular process that mediates the lysosomal degradation and relocation of cellular cargoes within double-membraned vesicles called autophagosomes.
source: Autophagy is a conserved eukaryotic cellular process that mediates the lysosomal degradation and relocation of cellular cargoes within double-membraned vesicles called autophagosomes (He and Klionsky, 2009; Leidal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Autophagy can be highly selective.
source: Although previously considered to be a bulk catabolic pathway tasked with maintaining cellular homeostasis under normal or stress conditions, it is now clear that autophagy can be highly selective (Zaffagnini and Martens, 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Autophagic cargoes are typically captured during autophagosome formation.
source: Autophagic cargoes are typically captured during autophagosome formation, a complex process regulated by a set of conserved autophagy-related proteins (ATG) as well as specialized autophagy adaptors and cargo receptors (Mizushima et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ATG8 decorates the phagophore to serve as a docking platform for cargo receptors.
source: These captured cargoes are sorted within the autophagosome during maturation of the isolation membrane (also known as the phagophore) via the specific interactions between cargo receptors and ATG8, which decorates the phagophore to serve as a docking platform for cargo receptors (Slobodkin and Elazar, 2013; Ryabovol and Minibayeva, 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The primary source of the phagophore is considered to be the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).
source: The source of the phagophore is still under debate, but its primary source is considered to be the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Bernard and Klionsky, 2013; Hamasaki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations, though noted as debated.

claim: The essential autophagy protein ATG2 has lipid transfer activity.
source: Supporting this view, the essential autophagy protein ATG2 was recently discovered to have lipid transfer activity (Valverde et al., 2019; Maeda et al., 2019; Osawa et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In yeast, lipids mobilized from lipid droplets were found to fuel autophagosome biogenesis during starvation-induced autophagy.
source: Remarkably, in yeast, lipids mobilized from lipid droplets (LDs) were found to fuel autophagosome biogenesis during starvation-induced autophagy, which employs relatively larger autophagosomes (Shpilka et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Smaller autophagosomes of the cytosol-to-vacuole targeting (Cvt) pathway do not rely on LDs.
source: In contrast, smaller autophagosomes of the cytosol-to-vacuole targeting (Cvt) pathway do not rely on LDs, suggesting that LDs are specifically recruited for starvation-induced autophagy in order to meet the increased demand of lipids required for the biogenesis of larger sized autophagosomes (Shpilka et al., 2015; Dupont et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Autophagosome maturation relies on vesicle transport and membrane expansion events which are regulated by secretory pathways involving Rab GTPases.
source: Although poorly characterized, there is accumulating evidence for autophagosome maturation relying on vesicle transport and membrane expansion events which are regulated by secretory pathways involving Rab GTPases (Ao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The mammalian Rab8a that regulates polarized secretion and lipid droplet fusion events is also implicated in autophagy.
source: For instance, the mammalian Rab8a that regulates polarized secretion and lipid droplet fusion events is also implicated in autophagy (Bansal et al., 2018; Vaibhava et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The model plant Arabidopsis genome contains five closely related Rab8a members organized into the RabE group (RabE1a-d).
source: The model plant Arabidopsis genome contains five closely related Rab8a members organized into the RabE group (RabE1a-d), but whether any of the RabE1 members contribute to autophagy is unknown (Rutherford and Moore, 2002).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The plant selective autophagy cargo receptor Joka2/NBR1 mediates antiviral immunity by eliminating viral components.
source: For instance, the plant selective autophagy cargo receptor Joka2/NBR1 mediates antiviral immunity by eliminating viral components (Hafrén et al., 2017; Hafrén et al., 2018; Jung et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Joka2/NBR1 is required for immunity against bacteria and oomycete pathogens.
source: Joka2/NBR1 is also required for immunity against bacteria and oomycete pathogens, however, the extent to which defense-related autophagy acts against these pathogens is unknown (Dagdas et al., 2018; Üstün et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Adapted pathogens have evolved strategies to manipulate the host autophagy machinery.
source: Consistent with the important role of autophagy in plant immunity, adapted pathogens have evolved strategies to manipulate the host autophagy machinery (Leary et al., 2018; Üstün et al., 2018; Leary et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Plants detect pathogens via immune sensors consisting of surface localized pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) and intracellular nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat-containing proteins (NLRs).
source: Plants detect pathogens via immune sensors consisting of surface localized pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) and intracellular nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat-containing proteins (NLRs).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about plant immunity.

claim: Pathogens secrete an arsenal of effector proteins to modulate host immunity and processes to support their virulence.
source: In response, pathogens secrete an arsenal of effector proteins to modulate host immunity and processes to support their virulence.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about pathogen-host interactions.

claim: Some filamentous plant pathogens produce hyphal extensions called haustoria that grow into the host cells to facilitate effector delivery and gain access to host nutrients.
source: Some filamentous plant pathogens, including the Irish potato famine pathogen Phytophthora infestans, produce hyphal extensions called haustoria that grow into the host cells to facilitate effector delivery and gain access to host nutrients (Panstruga and Dodds, 2009).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A haustorium is a specialized infection structure that remains enveloped by an enigmatic host-derived membrane known as the extra-haustorial membrane (EHM).
source: A haustorium is a specialized infection structure that remains enveloped by an enigmatic host-derived membrane known as the extra-haustorial membrane (EHM), whose functions and biogenesis are poorly understood (Whisson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Joka2-mediated defense-related autophagy is diverted to the EHM during P. infestans infection.
source: Notably, we previously showed that Joka2-mediated defense-related autophagy is diverted to the EHM during P. infestans infection (Dagdas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 is a host-translocated RXLR class of effector with five consecutive WY motifs that targets plant autophagy.
source: The pathogen counteracts this by deploying PexRD54, a host-translocated RXLR class of effector with five consecutive WY motifs, that targets plant autophagy (Dagdas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 carries a canonical C-terminal ATG8 interacting motif (AIM) that is typically found on autophagy cargo receptors to bind ATG8.
source: PexRD54 carries a canonical C-terminal ATG8 interacting motif (AIM) that is typically found on autophagy cargo receptors to bind ATG8 (Maqbool et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a previous finding supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 preferentially binds the ATG8CL isoform among the diverse set of potato ATG8 members.
source: Among the diverse set of potato ATG8 members (Kellner et al., 2017; Zess et al., 2019), PexRD54 preferentially binds the ATG8CL isoform and outcompetes Joka2/NBR1 from ATG8CL complexes, thereby disarming defense-related autophagy at the pathogen interface (Dagdas et al., 2016; Dagdas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 outcompetes Joka2/NBR1 from ATG8CL complexes, thereby disarming defense-related autophagy at the pathogen interface.
source: Among the diverse set of potato ATG8 members (Kellner et al., 2017; Zess et al., 2019), PexRD54 preferentially binds the ATG8CL isoform and outcompetes Joka2/NBR1 from ATG8CL complexes, thereby disarming defense-related autophagy at the pathogen interface (Dagdas et al., 2016; Dagdas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 does not fully shutdown autophagy as has been shown for animal pathogens that suppress autophagy.
source: Intriguingly, PexRD54 does not fully shutdown autophagy as has been shown for animal pathogens that suppress autophagy (Choy et al., 2012; Kimmey and Stallings, 2016; Real et al., 2018; Xu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 stimulates formation of autophagosomes that accumulate around the pathogen interface.
source: Instead, it stimulates formation of autophagosomes that accumulate around the pathogen interface (Dagdas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 couples the host vesicle transport regulator Rab8a to autophagosome biogenesis at the pathogen interface.
source: Here, we show that PexRD54 mimics carbon starvation-induced autophagy by coupling the host vesicle transport regulator Rab8a (Speth et al., 2009; Zheng et al., 2005; Pfeffer, 2017) to autophagosome biogenesis at the pathogen interface.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: PexRD54 activates autophagy by recruiting Rab8a to ATG8CL compartments.
source: Unlike PexRD54 which activates autophagy by recruiting Rab8a to ATG8CL compartments, PexRD54's AIM peptide fails to associate with Rab8a, and instead functions as an autophagy inhibitor.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: PexRD54's AIM peptide fails to associate with Rab8a and instead functions as an autophagy inhibitor.
source: Unlike PexRD54 which activates autophagy by recruiting Rab8a to ATG8CL compartments, PexRD54's AIM peptide fails to associate with Rab8a, and instead functions as an autophagy inhibitor.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: PexRD54 stimulates formation of ATG8CL-autophagosomes in a macroautophagy dependent manner.
source: We have previously shown that PexRD54 stimulates formation of ATG8CL-autophagosomes in a macroautophagy dependent manner, and PexRD54 itself is a substrate of host autophagy when expressed in plant cells (Dagdas et al., 2016; Maqbool et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: PexRD54 itself is a substrate of host autophagy when expressed in plant cells.
source: We have previously shown that PexRD54 stimulates formation of ATG8CL-autophagosomes in a macroautophagy dependent manner, and PexRD54 itself is a substrate of host autophagy when expressed in plant cells (Dagdas et al., 2016; Maqbool et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: During infection, pathogen-induced autophagosomes are diverted to the EHM in a process that relies on the core autophagy machinery.
source: During infection, these pathogen-induced autophagosomes are diverted to the EHM in a process that relies on the core autophagy machinery (Dagdas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: AIM-mediated binding of PexRD54 to ATG8CL is essential for the activation of autophagosome formation by the effector protein.
source: Because AIM-mediated binding of PexRD54 to ATG8CL is essential for the activation of autophagosome formation by the effector protein (Dagdas et al., 2016; Maqbool et al., 2016), we reasoned that PexRD54 could stimulate autophagosome formation by either negative regulation of host autophagy suppressors or through positive regulation of host components to the autophagosome biogenesis sites.
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: RFP:AIMp significantly reduced the number of GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes in leaf epidermal cells.
source: Strikingly, instead of stimulating autophagosome formation, AIMp fused to RFP (RFP:AIMp) significantly reduced the number of ATG8CL-autophagosomes in leaf epidermal cells (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Compared to RFP:GUS control, expression of RFP:AIMp reduced the number of GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes by ~sixfold.
source: Compared to RFP:GUS control, expression of RFP:AIMp reduced the number of GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes by ~sixfold, whereas cells expressing RFP:PexRD54 had a ~fourfold increase in GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosome numbers as has been shown before (Figure 1A–B; Dagdas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Cells expressing RFP:PexRD54 had a ~fourfold increase in GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosome numbers.
source: Compared to RFP:GUS control, expression of RFP:AIMp reduced the number of GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes by ~sixfold, whereas cells expressing RFP:PexRD54 had a ~fourfold increase in GFP:ATG8CL-autophagosome numbers as has been shown before (Figure 1A–B; Dagdas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-B and previous citations.

claim: The AIMp interacted with ATG8CL in planta.
source: The AIMp interacted with ATG8CL in planta (Figure 1C–D), as was previously shown through in vitro studies (Dagdas et al., 2016; Maqbool et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C-D and previous citations.

claim: Binding of PexRD54 to ATG8CL, although necessary, is not sufficient to activate autophagosome biogenesis.
source: Taken together these results show that binding of PexRD54 to ATG8CL, although necessary, is not sufficient to activate autophagosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMp binds ATG8CL but does not activate autophagy.

claim: The full-length PexRD54 protein stimulates autophagy while PexRD54's AIM peptide functions as an autophagy suppressor.
source: This suggests while the full-length protein stimulates autophagy, PexRD54's AIM peptide functions as an autophagy suppressor.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential effects of full-length PexRD54 and AIMp on autophagy.

claim: RFP:AIMp stabilized GFP:ATG8CL compared to RFP:PexRD54 or the controls RFP:EV and RFP:GUS.
source: Consistent with the AIMp triggered decrease in ATG8CL-autophagosome numbers (Figure 1A–B), RFP:AIMp stabilized GFP:ATG8CL compared to RFP:PexRD54 or the controls RFP:EV and RFP:GUS (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the presence of RFP:AIMp, GFP:ATG8CL was still able to produce a strong protein signal even after 6 days of transient expression.
source: Western blotting showed that in the presence of RFP:AIMp, GFP:ATG8CL was still able to produce a strong protein signal even after 6 days of transient expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: GFP:ATG8CL protein signal was hardly detectable after just four days in the presence of RFP:PexRD54 or RFP:EV.
source: On the other hand, GFP:ATG8CL protein signal was hardly detectable after just four days in the presence of RFP:PexRD54 or RFP:EV, indicating that the AIMp hampers autophagic flux (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PexRD54 acts as a cargo receptor that activates autophagy.
source: Consistent with our previous report that PexRD54 acts as a cargo receptor that activates autophagy (Dagdas et al., 2016), we saw rapid decline of RFP:PexRD54 protein levels after 2 days post infiltration (dpi) with only free RFP detectable at six dpi, indicating vacuolar processing of RFP:PexRD54 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations and experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: RFP:PexRD54 localizes to the cytoplasm at two dpi, but RFP signal becomes vacuolar at 4 and 6 dpi.
source: In line with this view, confocal microscopy revealed that while RFP:PexRD54 localizes to the cytoplasm at two dpi, RFP signal becomes vacuolar at 4 and 6 dpi (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), providing further evidence that PexRD54 itself is a substrate of autophagy and is degraded inside the plant vacuole, consistent with the flux assays we reported earlier (Dagdas et al., 2016; Maqbool et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and previous citations.

claim: RFP:AIMp remains mostly cytoplasmic at 2–6 dpi consistent with its function as a suppressor of ATG8 autophagy.
source: In contrast, RFP:AIMp remains mostly cytoplasmic at 2–6 dpi consistent with its function as a suppressor of ATG8 autophagy (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The AIM peptide mutated in the conserved ATG8-interacting region was unable to prevent ATG8CL depletion.
source: Moreover, the AIM peptide mutated in the conserved ATG8-interacting region was unable to prevent ATG8CL depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Inhibition of autophagy by AIMp relies on ATG8 binding.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that inhibition of autophagy by AIMp relies on ATG8 binding and AIMp can potentially block ATG8 dependent autophagy pathways.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that mutant AIMp that cannot bind ATG8 does not inhibit autophagy.

claim: RFP:AIMp showed a robust stabilization of all six potato ATG8 isoforms.
source: RFP:AIMp showed a robust stabilization of all six potato ATG8 isoforms (Figure 2B), demonstrating that AIMp acts as a broad spectrum autophagy suppressor.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: AIMp acts as a broad spectrum autophagy suppressor.
source: RFP:AIMp showed a robust stabilization of all six potato ATG8 isoforms (Figure 2B), demonstrating that AIMp acts as a broad spectrum autophagy suppressor.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMp stabilizes all six potato ATG8 isoforms.

claim: Ectopic expression of RFP:AIMp led to marked increase in both native NbJoka2 and NbATG8(s) levels compared to RFP:GUS expression.
source: Consistently, ectopic expression of RFP:AIMp led to marked increase in both native NbJoka2 and NbATG8(s) levels compared to RFP:GUS expression, whereas RFP:PexRD54 mildly increased levels of native NbJoka2 but not NbATG8s (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5A.

claim: RFP:PexRD54 mildly increased levels of native NbJoka2 but not NbATG8s.
source: Consistently, ectopic expression of RFP:AIMp led to marked increase in both native NbJoka2 and NbATG8(s) levels compared to RFP:GUS expression, whereas RFP:PexRD54 mildly increased levels of native NbJoka2 but not NbATG8s (Figure 2—figure supplement 5A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5A.

claim: PexRD54's AIMp suppresses autophagy non-selectively, whereas PexRD54 activates ATG8CL-autophagy while neutralizing Joka2-mediated autophagy.
source: These results further support the view that PexRD54's AIMp suppresses autophagy non-selectively, whereas PexRD54 activates ATG8CL-autophagy while neutralizing Joka2-mediated autophagy as shown before (Dagdas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data and previous citations.

claim: Only the wild-type AIMpsyn reduced the frequency of GFP:ATG8CL-puncta (by ~10-fold) compared to mAIMpsyn or buffer control in root cells.
source: Although both AIMpsyn and mAIMpsyn fused to 5-Carboxyfluorescein (CF-AIMpsyn and CF-mAIMpsyn) were effectively taken up by the root cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 6), only the wild-type AIMpsyn reduced the frequency of GFP:ATG8CL-puncta (by ~10-fold) compared to mAIMpsyn or buffer control (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: PexRD54's AIM peptide suppresses autophagy in a variety of tissues.
source: These findings demonstrate that PexRD54's AIM peptide suppresses autophagy in a variety of tissues, likely through binding to plant ATG8 isoforms with a high affinity and limiting their access to the autophagy adaptors that are essential for induction of autophagy.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMpsyn suppresses autophagy in both root and leaf cells.

claim: Full-length PexRD54 carries additional features to stimulate autophagosome formation, by for instance, recruiting and/or manipulating other host components.
source: This implies that full-length PexRD54 carries additional features to stimulate autophagosome formation, by for instance, recruiting and/or manipulating other host components.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMp alone does not stimulate autophagy.

claim: PexRD54 associates with Rab8a in planta.
source: We first validated PexRD54-Rab8a association through co-immunoprecipitation assays by co-expressing the potato Rab8a (herein Rab8a) or the N. benthamiana Rab8a (NbRab8a) with PexRD54 in planta (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The AIM mutant of PexRD54 (PexRD54AIM) that cannot bind ATG8CL still interacted with Rab8a to a similar degree as PexRD54.
source: Notably, the AIM mutant of PexRD54 (PexRD54AIM) that cannot bind ATG8CL still interacted with Rab8a to a similar degree as PexRD54 (Figure 3A), indicating that PexRD54 associates with Rab8a independent of its ATG8CL-binding activity.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: PexRD54 associates with Rab8a independent of its ATG8CL-binding activity.
source: Notably, the AIM mutant of PexRD54 (PexRD54AIM) that cannot bind ATG8CL still interacted with Rab8a to a similar degree as PexRD54 (Figure 3A), indicating that PexRD54 associates with Rab8a independent of its ATG8CL-binding activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that PexRD54AIM still binds Rab8a.

claim: The AIMp failed to associate with Rab8a in pull down assays, although it still strongly interacted with ATG8CL.
source: Consistent with this, the AIMp failed to associate with Rab8a in pull down assays, although it still strongly interacted with ATG8CL (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: PexRD54's N-terminal region preceding the C-terminal AIM mediates Rab8a association.
source: These results suggest that PexRD54's N-terminal region preceding the C-terminal AIM mediates Rab8a association.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMp does not bind Rab8a but full-length PexRD54 does.

claim: Both stably and transiently expressed Rab8a fused to GFP (GFP:Rab8a) produced fluorescent signals at both the plasma membrane and the vacuolar membrane (tonoplast).
source: Both stably and transiently expressed Rab8a fused to GFP (GFP:Rab8a) produced fluorescent signals at both the plasma membrane and the vacuolar membrane (tonoplast) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: GFP:Rab8a localized to mobile puncta (0.2–0.5 μm in diameter) as well as to larger ring-shaped structures.
source: In addition, GFP:Rab8a localized to mobile puncta (0.2–0.5 μm in diameter) as well as to larger ring-shaped structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Video 1), indicating that Rab8a could be involved in multiple cellular trafficking events.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Video 1.

claim: A subset of punctate structures labeled by GFP:Rab8a showed a clear overlap with RFP:PexRD54-puncta.
source: In line with the pull-down assays (Figure 3A–B), a subset of punctate structures labeled by GFP:Rab8a showed a clear overlap with RFP:PexRD54-puncta, whereas we did not detect any RFP signal peaking at GFP:Rab8a puncta in cells expressing RFP:AIMp or RFP:GUS (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PexRD54 associates with Rab8a in an AIM independent manner.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that PexRD54 associates with Rab8a in an AIM independent manner and raise the possibility that Rab8a could be an important component of PexRD54 driven autophagy.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMp does not bind Rab8a but full-length PexRD54 does.

claim: Rab8aS29N pulled-down PexRD54 more than wild type GFP:Rab8a or GFP:Rab8aQ74L in planta.
source: Rab8aS29N pulled-down PexRD54 more than wild type GFP:Rab8a or GFP:Rab8aQ74L in planta (Figure 3D), suggesting that PexRD54 preferentially associates with the GDP bound state of Rab8a (S29N).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: PexRD54 preferentially associates with the GDP bound state of Rab8a (S29N).
source: Rab8aS29N pulled-down PexRD54 more than wild type GFP:Rab8a or GFP:Rab8aQ74L in planta (Figure 3D), suggesting that PexRD54 preferentially associates with the GDP bound state of Rab8a (S29N).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that Rab8aS29N binds PexRD54 more strongly.

claim: BFP:PexRD54, but not free BFP or BFP:AIMp, localizes to puncta co-labeled by RFP:ATG8CL and GFP:Rab8a.
source: This revealed that BFP:PexRD54, but not free BFP or BFP:AIMp, localizes to puncta co-labeled by RFP:ATG8CL and GFP:Rab8a (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: GFP:Rab8a localized to ring-shaped RFP:ATG8CL clusters triggered by BFP:PexRD54.
source: Furthermore, GFP:Rab8a localized to ring-shaped RFP:ATG8CL clusters triggered by BFP:PexRD54, whereas no such structures occurred in cells expressing BFP control or BFP:AIMp (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Even in the absence of PexRD54, more than half of RFP:ATG8CL-puncta (60%, N = 18 images) are positively labeled by GFP:Rab8a.
source: Notably, our quantitative imaging revealed that, even in the absence of PexRD54, more than half of RFP:ATG8CL-puncta (60%, N = 18 images) are positively labeled by GFP:Rab8a (Figure 4A,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,D.

claim: BFP:PexRD54 expression significantly increased the frequency of GFP:Rab8a-positive RFP:ATG8CL-puncta (85%, N = 18 images).
source: However, BFP:PexRD54 expression significantly increased the frequency of GFP:Rab8a-positive RFP:ATG8CL-puncta (85%, N = 18 images) (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B,D.

claim: A subset of Rab8a localizes to autophagy compartments marked by ATG8CL and this is enhanced by PexRD54.
source: These results indicate that a subset of Rab8a localizes to autophagy compartments marked by ATG8CL and this is enhanced by PexRD54.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing increased colocalization of Rab8a and ATG8CL in the presence of PexRD54.

claim: Noticeably more RFP:ATG8CL pulled down with GFP:Rab8a in presence of 3xHA:PexRD54 but not 3xHA:AIMp or 3xHA:EV.
source: We observed noticeably more RFP:ATG8CL pulled down with GFP:Rab8a in presence of 3xHA:PexRD54 but not 3xHA:AIMp or 3xHA:EV (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: PexRD54 enhances Rab8a accumulation at ATG8CL-autophagosomes.
source: Altogether, these results show that PexRD54 enhances Rab8a accumulation at ATG8CL-autophagosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing increased colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation of Rab8a and ATG8CL in the presence of PexRD54.

claim: Expression of BFP:PexRD54 increases the proximity of ATG9 and Rab8a puncta (68%, N = 44 images quantified) compared to a BFP control (38%, N = 31 images quantified).
source: Confocal micrographs of haustoriated plant cells showed accumulation of RFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes around the haustoria which are co-labeled with GFP:Rab8a, and are positive for BFP:PexRD54 but not BFP control (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: PexRD54 stimulates association of Rab8a with the autophagosome biogenesis machinery.
source: Notably, in the presence of BFP:PexRD54, but not BFP:AIMp or BFP:EV, ATG9:GFP puncta showed more proximity to RFP:Rab8a puncta (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing increased proximity of ATG9 and Rab8a in the presence of PexRD54.

claim: PexRD54 promotes Rab8a recruitment to autophagosome biogenesis sites.
source: These results implicate Rab8a in autophagy and indicate that PexRD54 promotes Rab8a recruitment to autophagosome biogenesis sites.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing increased association of Rab8a with autophagy markers in the presence of PexRD54.

claim: Silencing of NbRab8a1-2 did not alter the number of RFP:ATG8CL puncta in the absence of PexRD54.
source: In the absence of PexRD54, silencing of NbRab8a1-2 did not alter the number of RFP:ATG8CL puncta (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Following stimulation of autophagy by transient expression of GFP:PexRD54, the number of RFP:ATG8CL-puncta/cell in RNAi:NbRab8a1-2 background reduced by half compared to a RNAi:GUS control.
source: However, following stimulation of autophagy by transient expression of GFP:PexRD54, the number of RFP:ATG8CL-puncta/cell in RNAi:NbRab8a1-2 background reduced by half compared to a RNAi:GUS control (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Simultaneous knockdown of NbRab8a1 and NbRab8a2 does not affect basal autophagy, but negatively impacts PexRD54-triggered autophagy.
source: This suggests that simultaneous knockdown of NbRab8a1 and NbRab8a2 does not affect basal autophagy, but negatively impacts PexRD54-triggered autophagy.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential effects of Rab8a silencing on basal and PexRD54-triggered autophagy.

claim: Rab8a positively regulates PexRD54-mediated autophagy.
source: These results suggest that Rab8a positively regulates PexRD54-mediated autophagy.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that Rab8a silencing reduces PexRD54-triggered autophagy.

claim: Knockdown of the four Rab8a isoforms using the RNAi:NbRab8a1-4 construct significantly reduced basal ATG8CL and PexRD54-triggered ATG8CL autophagosome numbers.
source: Intriguingly, knockdown of the four Rab8a isoforms using the RNAi:NbRab8a1-4 construct significantly reduced basal ATG8CL (Figure 5—figure supplement 5) and PexRD54-triggered ATG8CL autophagosome numbers (Figure 5—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5 and 6.

claim: GFP:Rab8aN128I led to 50% reduction in PexRD54 triggered ATG8CL-autophagosome numbers compared to wild-type GFP:Rab8a.
source: Consistent with the silencing assays (Figure 5A–D), GFP:Rab8aN128I led to 50% reduction in PexRD54 triggered ATG8CL-autophagosome numbers compared to wild-type GFP:Rab8a (Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 7.

claim: Expression of GDP-bound GFP:Rab8aS29N substantially enhanced (~three fold) the frequency of BFP:PexRD54 puncta compared to a GFP control.
source: Expression of GDP-bound GFP:Rab8aS29N substantially enhanced (~three fold) the frequency of BFP:PexRD54 puncta compared to a GFP control, whereas GTP bound GFP:Rab8aQ74L did not lead to any significant changes in the number of BFP:PexRD54 puncta compared to the GFP control (Figure 5—figure supplement 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 9.

claim: PexRD54-driven autophagy requires Rab8a.
source: Therefore, further biochemical evidence is required to determine whether these mutations show perturbed GTPase activities. Nevertheless, together with the data presented in Figure 3D, these findings demonstrate that PexRD54-driven autophagy requires Rab8a.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that Rab8a silencing and dominant negative Rab8a reduce PexRD54-triggered autophagy.

claim: Joka2 did not colocalize or interact with Rab8a.
source: Unlike PexRD54, Joka2 did not colocalize or interact with Rab8a (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Joka2 overexpression leads to a reduction of RFP:ATG8CL puncta positively labeled by GFP:Rab8a.
source: Moreover, our quantitative imaging revealed that Joka2 overexpression leads to a reduction of RFP:ATG8CL puncta positively labeled by GFP:Rab8a (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: The autophagy pathway mediated by Joka2 is different from the PexRD54 triggered autophagy, and possibly does not require Rab8a function.
source: This sharply contrasts with the positive impact of PexRD54 on ATG8CL-Rab8a association (Figure 6C,D), indicating that the autophagy pathway mediated by Joka2 is different from the PexRD54 triggered autophagy, and possibly does not require Rab8a function.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential effects of Joka2 and PexRD54 on Rab8a-ATG8CL association.

claim: No difference was detected in formation of Joka2-triggered autophagosomes upon NbRab8a1-2 silencing compared to GUS silencing.
source: Supporting this, we did not detect any difference in formation of Joka2-triggered autophagosomes upon NbRab8a1-2 silencing compared to GUS silencing (Figure 6E–F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E-F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Joka2-mediated autophagy pathway does not involve Rab8a.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that Joka2-mediated autophagy pathway does not involve Rab8a, and the weak association between ATG8CL and Rab8a observed in the absence of PexRD54 is not mediated by Joka2 but potentially through an unknown autophagy adaptor.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that Rab8a silencing does not affect Joka2-triggered autophagy.

claim: A slight yet significant increase in the number of RFP:ATG8CL puncta was detected upon incubation of plants for 24 hr in the dark compared to normal light conditions.
source: We detected a slight yet significant increase in the number of RFP:ATG8CL puncta upon incubation of plants for 24 hr in the dark compared to normal light conditions (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: When GFP:PexRD54 is present, no further enhancement of RFP:ATG8CL puncta was measured following 24 hr in the dark.
source: However, when GFP:PexRD54 is present, we did not measure any further enhancement of RFP:ATG8CL puncta following 24 hr in the dark, suggesting that PexRD54-mediated autophagy can override or mask starvation-induced autophagy (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: In plants stably expressing GFP:Rab8a that are light restricted, an increased degree of colocalization between RFP:ATG8CL and GFP:Rab8a was detected.
source: Furthermore, in plants stably expressing GFP:Rab8a that are light restricted, we detected an increased degree of colocalization between RFP:ATG8CL and GFP:Rab8a (Figure 7C–D, Figure 7—figure supplement 2), in a similar fashion to enhanced ATG8CL-Rab8a association mediated by PexRD54 (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C-D and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: PexRD54 mimics carbon-starvation-induced autophagy.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that PexRD54 mimics carbon-starvation-induced autophagy.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing similar effects of PexRD54 and light restriction on Rab8a-ATG8CL association.

claim: Ring-shaped PexRD54 clusters labeled with Rab8a also tightly associate with BODIPY-C12 labeled puncta.
source: Additionally, we observed that ring-shaped PexRD54 clusters labeled with Rab8a also tightly associate with BODIPY-C12 labeled puncta (Figure 7G, Figure 7—figure supplements 5–6).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7G and Figure 7—figure supplements 5-6.

claim: Fatty acids could be one of the potential membrane sources of the autophagosomes stimulated by PexRD54.
source: These findings suggest that fatty acids could be one of the potential membrane sources of the autophagosomes stimulated by PexRD54 as observed during carbon-starvation-induced autophagy in other systems (Shpilka et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculated based on the experimental data showing association of PexRD54 with lipid droplets and citations.

claim: Stimulation of autophagy by BFP:PexRD54, but not Joka2:BFP, led to enhanced association of BODIPY-C12 and GFP:Rab8a-labeled puncta.
source: Strikingly, stimulation of autophagy by BFP:PexRD54, but not Joka2:BFP, led to enhanced association of BODIPY-C12 and GFP:Rab8a-labeled puncta, supporting the hypothesis that PexRD54 mimics autophagy induced during carbon starvation (Figure 7H, Figure 7—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7H and Figure 7—figure supplement 7.

claim: PexRD54 triggers responses similar to carbon-starvation-induced autophagy including induction of autophagosomes and enhanced association of ATG8CL-autophagosomes with Rab8a and LDs.
source: Together these results show that unlike the aggrephagy receptor Joka2, PexRD54 triggers responses similar to carbon-starvation-induced autophagy including induction of autophagosomes and enhanced association of ATG8CL-autophagosomes with Rab8a and LDs (Figure 6 and Figure 7).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing similar effects of PexRD54 and carbon starvation on autophagy.

claim: Rab8a knockdown not only reduces the total amount of PexRD54 autophagosomes but also the proportion of those associated with LDs compared to a silencing control.
source: We observed that Rab8a knockdown not only reduces the total amount of PexRD54 autophagosomes but also the proportion of those associated with LDs compared to a silencing control (Figure 7—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 8.

claim: NbSeipin-A knockdown significantly reduced the amount of Oleosin-labeled LDs compared to a silencing control.
source: RNAi-mediated knockdown of the NbSeipin-A significantly reduced the amount of Oleosin-labeled LDs compared to a silencing control (Figure 7—figure supplements 9–10) consistent with the established role of Seipin in LD biogenesis.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplements 9-10.

claim: NbSeipin-A knockdown significantly reduced the amount of PexRD54 puncta in the cell compared to the control.
source: NbSeipin-A knockdown significantly reduced the amount of PexRD54 puncta in the cell compared to the control (Figure 7—figure supplement 11), supporting the notion that PexRD54 relies on host LD resources to stimulate autophagosome formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 11.

claim: PexRD54 requires Rab8a to recruit lipid droplets and LDs contribute to its induction of autophagosome formation.
source: Together, these data show that PexRD54 requires Rab8a to recruit lipid droplets and that LDs contribute to its induction of autophagosome formation.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that Rab8a and Seipin knockdown reduce PexRD54-triggered autophagy.

claim: The perihaustorial niche is a hot spot for the formation of ATG8CL autophagosomes stimulated by PexRD54.
source: Our recent work revealed that the perihaustorial niche is a hot spot for the formation of ATG8CL autophagosomes stimulated by PexRD54 (Dagdas et al., 2016; Dagdas et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by citations.

claim: In infected leaf epidermal cells transiently or stably expressing GFP:Rab8a, varying sizes of GFP:Rab8a puncta were detected around the P. infestans haustoria.
source: In infected leaf epidermal cells transiently or stably expressing GFP:Rab8a, we detected varying sizes of GFP:Rab8a puncta around the P. infestans haustoria (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Confocal micrographs of haustoriated plant cells showed accumulation of RFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes around the haustoria which are co-labeled with GFP:Rab8a, and are positive for BFP:PexRD54 but not BFP control.
source: Confocal micrographs of haustoriated plant cells showed accumulation of RFP:ATG8CL-autophagosomes around the haustoria which are co-labeled with GFP:Rab8a, and are positive for BFP:PexRD54 but not BFP control (Figure 8A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A-C.

claim: Formation of perihaustorial puncta co-labeled by RFP:ATG8CL and GFP:Rab8a was suppressed by arresting autophagosome formation through expression of BFP:AIMp.
source: However, formation of perihaustorial puncta co-labeled by RFP:ATG8CL and GFP:Rab8a was suppressed by arresting autophagosome formation through expression of BFP:AIMp (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: A subset of perihaustorial GFP:Rab8a puncta are not labeled by RFP:ATG8CL, further supporting an ATG8CL-independent haustorial trafficking role for Rab8a.
source: Notably, we detected a subset of perihaustorial GFP:Rab8a puncta that are not labeled by RFP:ATG8CL, further supporting an ATG8CL-independent haustorial trafficking role for Rab8a (Figure 8A–D, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A-D and Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rab8a localization to Golgi around the haustorium is in agreement with the conserved role of Rab8 in yeast and metazoans to mediate polarized secretion of proteins.
source: Localization of Rab8a to Golgi around the haustorium is in agreement with the conserved role of Rab8 in yeast and metazoans to mediate polarized secretion of proteins (Nielsen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Simultaneous RNAi-mediated knockdown of all four NbRab8a members led to a consistent increase in disease symptoms and P. infestans hyphal growth.
source: Simultaneous RNAi-mediated knockdown of all four NbRab8a members led to a consistent increase in disease symptoms and P. infestans hyphal growth (Figure 8—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 6.

claim: The enhanced susceptibility phenotype caused by RNAi:NbRab8a1-4 silencing was rescued by simultaneous overexpression of GFP:Rab8asyn but not the GFP control.
source: The enhanced susceptibility phenotype caused by RNAi:NbRab8a1-4 silencing was rescued by simultaneous overexpression of GFP:Rab8asyn but not the GFP control, providing further evidence that Rab8a is required for basal resistance against P. infestans (Figure 8—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 7.

claim: Overexpression of dominant negative GFP:Rab8aN128I enhanced plant susceptibility to P. infestans compared to a GFP control.
source: Consistent with knockdown assays, overexpression of dominant negative GFP:Rab8aN128I enhanced plant susceptibility to P. infestans compared to a GFP control (Figure 8—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 8.

claim: Rab8a contributes to plant immunity.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that Rab8a contributes to plant immunity, whereas PexRD54 could possibly interfere with the defense-related role of Rab8a by subverting a subpopulation of it to autophagic compartments.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that Rab8a knockdown increases susceptibility to P. infestans.

claim: Transient expression of RFP:AIMp led to ~threefold decrease in the number of haustoria that are associated with autophagosomes marked by GFP:ATG8CL compared to RFP:PexRD54 expression.
source: Our quantitative image analysis revealed that compared to RFP:PexRD54 expression, transient expression of RFP:AIMp led to ~threefold decrease in the number of haustoria that are associated with autophagosomes marked by GFP:ATG8CL (Figure 9A–B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A-B.

claim: N. benthamiana leaf patches expressing RFP:AIMp showed a consistent reduction of quantitative disease symptoms compared to an RFP vector control.
source: In multiple independent experiments (six biological replicates), N. benthamiana leaf patches expressing RFP:AIMp showed a consistent reduction of quantitative disease symptoms compared to an RFP vector control (Figure 9C–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9C-D.

claim: AIMp-mediated arrest of host autophagy negatively impacts P. infestans virulence.
source: This indicated that AIMp-mediated arrest of host autophagy negatively impacts P. infestans virulence, supporting the hypothesis that PexRD54-triggered autophagy is beneficial to the pathogen.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that AIMp expression reduces disease symptoms.

claim: P. infestans relies on host autophagy function to support its virulence.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that P. infestans relies on host autophagy function to support its virulence.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that autophagy inhibition reduces pathogen virulence.
